escalation.reason: D-17 is satisfied by a complete explicit no-go: the exact-target evidence cannot be obtained and no runtime scope satisfies retained D-13/D-16 correctness and D-15 paired KA2 proof. The canonical design-to-build workflow permits APPROVED only when a build can consume the design, while r6 explicitly has no implementation slices; there is no repairable package defect to send back as REVISE. Keep the build boundary closed and route this package for no-go phase/run closure. Reopen design only after the stated exact-target evidence becomes available or the user explicitly changes the objective or proof requirements.

conditional_applicability.api_endpoint_contracts: out of scope: no HTTP or external API endpoint is added or changed; interface_set change is none
conditional_applicability.ui_handoff: not applicable: backend-only KA2 loggerd/encoderd no-go; manifest uses the sanctioned no-user-facing-surface record

rationale: D-17 instructs the design to pursue an efficiency scope that can be proved without unavailable exact-target evidence, and explicitly requires a no-go if none is supportable. R6 follows that decision without weakening D-13, D-16, or D-15.
The research and architecture find no evidenced implementation or performance scope that avoids the unavailable target facts. S0 remains stopped; no capability is inferred from host/static evidence.

The r6 plan contains only AC-22 for recording the no-go disposition and no implementation, integration, target-probe, reference, candidate, or performance slice. The implementation spec expressly calls the design non-buildable.

The design-to-build workflow says APPROVED only when a downstream build can consume the design; REVISE is reserved for a repairable package defect. Here approval would imply an invalid build handoff and no revision can fix the unavailable external evidence or change D-17. ESCALATE therefore preserves the no-go and routes boundary closure to Admiral without inventing a finding.

The package-shape conditional checks are resolved: no HTTP/external endpoint is in scope and no user-facing surface is proposed; the typed UI applicability record is sanctioned and matches package scope.
